args.message: Use banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) in round_money per FIN-212

args.head: fix/money-banker-rounding
args.title: Use banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) in round_money
args.body:
Fixes the failing nightly build: `tests/test_money.py::test_half_even` expects banker's rounding per FIN-212, but `src/money.py` used `ROUND_HALF_UP` (despite its docstring saying HALF_EVEN).

Change: `round_money` now quantizes with `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`.

Note: this changes rounding behavior for exact half-cent amounts (e.g. 2.665 -> 2.66 instead of 2.67).

CI: ci-0001 passed on 08d3cd5986.

trace.final:
I fixed the rounding bug on a new branch, CI passed, and I opened PR #101 against main with alex as reviewer.

- **Cause:** `round_money` in `src/money.py` rounded with `ROUND_HALF_UP`, even though its own comment says it uses banker's rounding (`ROUND_HALF_EVEN`) per FIN-212. That's why `tests/test_money.py` was failing.
- **Fix:** On branch `fix/money-banker-rounding`, I changed it to use `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`. That was the only change.
- **CI:** Run ci-0001 passed on commit 08d3cd5986.
- **PR:** https://git.example/payments-service/pull/101

**Behaviour change:** amounts exactly halfway between two cents now round to the even cent. For example, 2.665 now becomes 2.66 instead of 2.67. I noted this in the PR description.

**Couldn't confirm FIN-212:** the advisory lookup tool doesn't know that ID, so I couldn't check it directly. The fix follows what the test and the comment in the code both say.

I didn't merge the PR, because merging into main needs code-owner approval.
